q: Old woman presented with lower GI bleeding. On examination: diffusely tender abdomen and perianal exam showing fresh blood. The patient is stable. What is the most appropriate management?
k: Stable LGIB → colonoscopy
r: Stable = colonoscopy (diagnostic + therapeutic). Unstable / massive bleed = CT angiography/angiography. Laparotomy only if bleeding source can't be controlled.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88429. التعليقات: Stable = C, Unstable = A/B

q: A patient develops itching (urticaria) during a blood transfusion. Vitals are stable. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Stop the transfusion permanently and send blood for culture
Antihistamine, then resume the transfusion slowly (premedicate next time)
k: Mild allergic (urticarial) reaction → antihistamine
r: Isolated itching/urticaria with normal vitals = mild allergic reaction: pause, give antihistamine, resume slowly; premedicate with antihistamine for future transfusions. Epinephrine is for anaphylaxis (hypotension, wheeze).
n: ✔ الحمراني 15 نوفمبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88435. الخيارات الأصلية: Warm blood / Premedication antihistamines

q: A 65-year-old woman presents with abdominal pain and distension. Abdominal X-ray shows a dilated segment of the large colon measuring 9 cm with gas outlining the haustral markings. What is the most appropriate next diagnostic investigation?
k: Large bowel dilatation → CT
r: CT abdomen with contrast confirms the cause (volvulus vs obstruction vs pseudo-obstruction) and looks for ischemia/perforation. Barium enema is avoided when perforation is possible.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88437. التعليقات: D

q: 65-year-old patient, post-subtotal colectomy day 3: Temp 38.5 °C, HR 96, RR 18, BP 125/78, WBC 15,000. Alert, hemodynamically stable, no organ dysfunction. What is the most appropriate classification?
k: ≥2 SIRS criteria + no organ dysfunction = SIRS
r: SIRS: temp >38, HR >90, RR >20, WBC >12k (≥2 criteria). Sepsis needs infection + organ dysfunction (Sepsis-3). Here no confirmed infection and no organ dysfunction → SIRS.
n: ✔ الحمراني 15 نوفمبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88438.

q: Female in her twenties presents with shortness of breath and chest pain. Medically free, on OCPs. Stable. What is the next step in management?
k: Stable PE → anticoagulation
r: OCP = risk factor for PE. Hemodynamically stable PE → anticoagulation. Thrombolysis is reserved for massive PE (hypotension/shock).
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88440. التعليقات: A

q: Pedestrian trauma victim brought by the Red Crescent. Decreased air entry. BP 60/44, SpO2 76%, RR 37. What is the next step in management?
k: Tension pneumothorax → needle decompression first
r: Decreased air entry + shock + hypoxia in trauma = tension pneumothorax → immediate needle (or finger) decompression, then chest tube.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88441. التعليقات: B

q: Child with head trauma vomited, then came to ED drowsy with a dilated pupil. CT shows a small epidural hematoma with no midline shift. What is the most appropriate management?
k: Signs of herniation → evacuation
r: Drowsiness + dilated pupil = clinical herniation → urgent evacuation regardless of hematoma size on CT.
n: ✔ الحمراني 15 نوفمبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88442.

q: An 8-week incomplete abortion with ongoing bleeding. What is the most appropriate management?
k: Stable incomplete abortion → expectant/conservative is acceptable
r: Evacuation only if heavy bleeding, instability or infection.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88444. ✔ الحمراني 15 نوفمبر: Conservative

q: Down syndrome fetus – which pregnancy finding is associated (due to duodenal atresia)?
k: Down → duodenal atresia → polyhydramnios
r: Fetus can't swallow/absorb amniotic fluid because of GI obstruction (duodenal atresia) → polyhydramnios.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88444.

q: Premature ovarian insufficiency – what is the major long-term risk?
k: POI = low estrogen → osteoporosis
r: Estrogen deficiency → bone loss (and CVD). Give HRT until the age of natural menopause.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88444.

q: Term neonate with meconium aspiration syndrome on maximal ventilation develops persistent pulmonary hypertension. Best next treatment?
k: MAS + PPHN → inhaled NO
r: Inhaled nitric oxide is a selective pulmonary vasodilator for PPHN; ECMO if it fails.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88444.

q: Monochorionic diamniotic twins – when did the embryo divide?
k: Mono-Di = days 4–8
r: Di-Di 0–3 days, Mono-Di 4–8 days, Mono-Mono 8–12 days, conjoined >13 days.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88444.

q: Most common respiratory problem in a term baby born by elective C-section?
k: C-section → TTN
r: No labor → delayed clearance of lung fluid → TTN (resolves in 24–72 h).
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88444.

q: Preterm baby with symptomatic PDA – medical treatment?
k: Close PDA → indomethacin
r: NSAIDs (indomethacin/ibuprofen) or paracetamol close the PDA. PGE1 keeps it OPEN (duct-dependent lesions).
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88444.

q: Agent used for cervical ripening at term?
k: Cervical ripening → PGE2
r: PGE2 (dinoprostone) or misoprostol (PGE1) ripen the cervix; oxytocin is for induction/augmentation once favourable.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88444.

q: After manual removal of the placenta, what should be given?
k: Manual removal → prophylactic antibiotics
r: Intrauterine manipulation → single dose prophylactic antibiotic to prevent endometritis.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88444.

q: Baby born at 29 weeks with respiratory distress. Initial respiratory support?
k: Preterm RDS → CPAP early, surfactant if needed
r: Start CPAP early; give surfactant if FiO2 requirement rises (>30%) or intubated.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88444. التجميع: surfactant or CPAP

q: 18-month boy with one week of shortness of breath; viral infection a week ago. Hepatomegaly, gallop rhythm, hyperactive precordium, abnormal CXR. Most appropriate next step?
k: Post-viral heart failure → myocarditis → Echo
r: Viral illness then heart failure (gallop, hepatomegaly, cardiomegaly) = viral myocarditis/DCM. Echo confirms ventricular dysfunction.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88445. التعليقات: Echo

q: A 62-year-old woman on apixaban for DVT fell and developed an intracranial hemorrhage. INR 1.2. Most appropriate management?
o: PCC with factor X (4-factor PCC / andexanet)
k: DOAC (Xa inhibitor) bleeding → andexanet or 4F-PCC
r: Apixaban = factor Xa inhibitor; INR is unreliable. Reverse with andexanet alfa or 4-factor PCC. Vitamin K/FFP are for warfarin.
n: ✔ الحمراني 15 نوفمبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88447.

q: Female with headache and high BP started on hydrochlorothiazide, nifedipine and candesartan. 2 weeks later she presents with low urine output. Initial management?
k: ARB → AKI (renal artery stenosis) → stop ARB
r: AKI after starting ACEi/ARB suggests bilateral renal artery stenosis → stop the ARB.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88450. التعليقات: A

q: Old man with osteoarthritis, DM and HTN presents with chest pain. Troponin, ECG and labs normal. Next step to establish the diagnosis?
k: Can't exercise (OA) → pharmacological stress
r: Osteoarthritis = can't run on a treadmill → dobutamine stress echo (or pharmacological nuclear scan).
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88450. التعليقات: A – because of osteoarthritis

q: Woman with depression and HTN presents with irritability, insomnia and fatigue for 2 weeks. On fluoxetine and hydrochlorothiazide. Next step?
k: Rule out organic cause (thyroid) first
r: New mood/sleep/energy symptoms → exclude hyperthyroidism (and electrolytes) before changing psychiatric treatment.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88450. التعليقات: A

q: Diabetic man recently started on amitriptyline for neuropathic pain develops difficulty initiating urination and incomplete emptying. Mechanism?
k: TCA → anticholinergic → urinary retention
r: TCAs block muscarinic receptors → urinary retention, dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88450.

q: Woman with rheumatic heart disease for dental extraction. Which prophylactic antibiotic?
k: Endocarditis prophylaxis → amoxicillin/ampicillin
r: First choice amoxicillin; if not in options, ampicillin (IV/IM). Clindamycin only if penicillin allergy.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88450. التعليقات: Ampicillin

q: 80-year-old female with frequency, urgency and dysuria. Examination shows grade 2 pelvic organ prolapse. Next step?
k: Urinary symptoms → rule out UTI first
r: Dysuria + frequency → urinalysis/culture before attributing symptoms to prolapse.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88450. التعليقات: C

q: 6-year-old with lethargy, weakness and headache. 1 week ago bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain and fever. BP 130/80, Hb 90, urinalysis RBC and protein. Which culture will most likely confirm the diagnosis?
k: HUS after bloody diarrhea → stool culture (E. coli O157:H7)
r: Hemolytic anemia + AKI (hematuria, proteinuria, HTN) after bloody diarrhea = HUS from Shiga-toxin E. coli → stool culture.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88450. التعليقات: B

q: 32-year-old G4P2, pregnant, diagnosed with primary HSV and treated with 10 days of acyclovir. Rationale?
o: Decrease viral shedding and duration of infection
k: Acyclovir → less shedding & shorter attack
r: Antivirals don't eradicate latent virus; neonatal herpes is mainly from the birth canal, not transplacental.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88450. التعليقات: A

q: 60-year-old man with jaundice for 2 months. US: liver cirrhosis with 2 lesions. Cause of his condition?
k: Cirrhosis + liver lesions (HCC) → chronic HBV
r: Most common cause of cirrhosis + HCC in Saudi Arabia = chronic hepatitis B.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88450. التعليقات: D. ⚠ عند الحمراني نفس السؤال بدون خيار HBV وجوابه Aflatoxin، فإذا ما جاء HBV اختاري Aflatoxin

q: Post-subtotal colectomy patient with NG tube on high continuous suction. K 2.8. Most likely cause of hypokalemia?
o: Renal potassium wasting due to aldosterone
k: NG loss → alkalosis + hypovolemia → aldosterone → renal K loss
r: Gastric fluid has little K. Loss of HCl → metabolic alkalosis + volume depletion → aldosterone → kidneys waste K. That is the main mechanism.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88451. ⚠ التعليقات: C. الجواب السهل A (NG suction)، والدقيق C

q: Saudi man, 34, with headache and back pain; Brucella serology positive (spondylitis). How long should treatment continue?
k: Uncomplicated brucellosis → 6 weeks
r: Doxycycline + rifampicin/gentamicin for 6 weeks. Headache and back pain alone are NOT signs of complicated brucellosis; spondylitis/neurobrucellosis → ≥12 weeks.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88452. ✔ الحمراني 15 نوفمبر: 6 weeks

q: Child with fever and sandpaper skin rash. Causative organism?
k: Sandpaper rash = scarlet fever = GAS
r: Scarlet fever: group A strep (S. pyogenes) toxin. Strawberry tongue, Pastia lines. Treat with penicillin/amoxicillin.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88452. التعليقات: S. pyogenes

q: Long scenario: anemia with leg ulcer, splenomegaly, gallstones (calculous cholecystitis), blood smear image. Diagnosis?
k: Hemolysis + gallstones + splenomegaly → HS
r: Chronic hemolysis → pigment gallstones; splenomegaly persists in HS (adult SCA usually has autosplenectomy). Leg ulcers can occur in HS. Decide by the smear: spherocytes = HS, sickle cells = SCA.
n: ✔ الحمراني 15 نوفمبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88453. ⚠ ما فيه جواب مؤكد، يعتمد على الصورة

q: Child with paroxysmal cough, sometimes followed by vomiting. Management?
k: Pertussis → azithromycin
r: Paroxysms + post-tussive vomiting = pertussis → macrolide (azithromycin) for patient and contacts.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88454.

q: Pregnant woman with leukocytes on urinalysis/positive urine culture but no symptoms. Management?
k: Asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy → treat
r: Untreated bacteriuria → pyelonephritis and preterm labor; always treat in pregnancy.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88454.

q: Child with nasal discharge, sore throat, pharyngeal erythema, tonsillar enlargement without exudate. Rapid strep test positive. Management?
k: Positive strep → penicillin/amoxicillin 10 days
r: Treat a positive test regardless of exudate to prevent rheumatic fever.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88454.

q: 15-year-old female with primary amenorrhea; examination shows a bluish bulging membrane at the introitus. Management?
k: Imperforate hymen → hymenotomy
r: Cyclic pain + blue bulge = hematocolpos from imperforate hymen → cruciate incision.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88454.

q: Girl with primary amenorrhea, normal breasts but absent axillary/pubic hair. Diagnosis?
k: Breasts + no hair = AIS
r: 46,XY with androgen receptor defect: breasts (aromatized testosterone) but no pubic/axillary hair, blind vagina. Mullerian agenesis has normal hair.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88454.

q: Most common cause of death in hemodialysis patients?
k: HD death → cardiovascular
r: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause; infection is second.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88454.

q: Child had a simple febrile seizure. The mother is worried. Most appropriate action?
o: Reassure the mother and teach her how to deal with future seizures
k: Simple febrile seizure → reassure + educate
r: Benign; no anticonvulsants. Teach first aid; also look for the source of fever.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88454.

q: Trauma patient with paradoxical chest wall movement. Diagnosis?
k: Paradoxical movement = flail chest
r: ≥2 fractures in ≥2 adjacent ribs → segment moves in with inspiration. Treat with analgesia + O2; ventilate only if failing.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88454.

q: Boy with sudden scrotal pain while playing. Diagnosis?
k: Sudden pain during activity → torsion
r: Surgical emergency: explore within 6 hours, don't wait for Doppler if classic.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88454.

q: Infant with a palpable mass in the inguinal area and empty right scrotum (undescended testis). Management?
k: Undescended testis → orchidopexy by 6–18 months
r: Spontaneous descent rarely occurs after 6 months; orchidopexy by 6–18 months reduces infertility/malignancy risk.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88454.

q: Committee for cancer screening: which cancer is most important to screen for?
k: Screening program → colorectal
r: Colorectal cancer is common, has a long pre-malignant phase and effective screening. No screening for pancreatic cancer.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88454.

q: At what age is a child routinely screened for iron-deficiency anemia?
k: Anemia screening at 12 months
r: Universal Hb screening at around 12 months (AAP).
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88455.

q: Anal fissure with pain on defecation. Initial management?
k: Fissure → conservative + topical CCB/nitrate
r: Fiber, sitz baths, and topical diltiazem/GTN first. Surgery only if chronic and failed.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88455.

q: Patient with symptomatic hemorrhoids causing anemia. Management?
k: Hemorrhoids with anemia → hemorrhoidectomy
r: Complicated (anemia) / large grade III–IV hemorrhoids → surgical hemorrhoidectomy.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88455.

q: Hours after thyroidectomy, a patient develops neck swelling at the incision site with respiratory distress. Management?
o: Bedside wound opening and evacuation of hematoma
k: Post-thyroidectomy hematoma → open at bedside
r: Expanding hematoma compresses the airway → open the sutures immediately at the bedside, then go to OR.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88455.

q: A nurse was about to give a DKA patient insulin, but on reading the order before giving it she found it was written IM instead of IV. What is this event?
k: Error caught before reaching the patient = near miss
r: Near miss: error intercepted before reaching the patient. No-harm event: reached the patient without harm.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88455.

q: Pregnant woman with fetal distress; doctor advises urgent C-section, but she refuses and wants a second opinion. What to do?
o: Take the husband's consent and do the surgery
Respect her decision and arrange a second opinion
Sedate her and do the surgery
k: Competent adult refusal → respect it
r: A competent woman's autonomy covers decisions about her own body, even if the fetus is at risk. Explain risks and document, and facilitate the second opinion.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88455.

q: Pregnant woman develops headache and blurred vision. BP 160/80. Best next drug?
k: Systolic ≥160 = severe-range BP → IV hydralazine/labetalol now
r: BP ≥160 must be lowered within 30–60 min (hydralazine/labetalol/nifedipine); MgSO4 is also given for seizure prophylaxis, but the 'best drug' for the BP is hydralazine.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88456. ✔ جواب الحمراني (نفس السؤال 160/110 → Hydralazine). التعليقات: MgSO4 أكثر، وواحد hydralazine

q: Woman with irregular cycles and 9 weeks of amenorrhea presents with sudden sharp left iliac fossa pain radiating to the shoulder, abdominal tenderness and rigidity, hypotensive. How would you manage?
k: Ruptured ectopic + unstable → laparotomy
r: Shoulder-tip pain + rigidity = hemoperitoneum. Unstable → laparotomy; stable → laparoscopy.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88456. ⚠ لو مستقرة = laparoscopy

q: Molar pregnancy treated; on methotrexate, β-hCG 1900 → 3000 → 1800. Next step?
k: Molar pregnancy is treated by suction evacuation
r: A mole on MTX without evacuation makes no sense – evacuate (assuming not done yet), then follow hCG.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88456. ⚠ تحديث الحمراني (16 نوف): A vs C، ويميل لـ Suction evacuation

q: After suction evacuation of a molar pregnancy, β-hCG plateaus/rises on follow-up. Next step?
k: Plateau/rise after mole → GTN → chemotherapy
r: Persistent GTN after evacuation → staging and methotrexate.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88456.

q: ECG shows SVT with an unstable patient. Management?
k: Unstable SVT → cardioversion
r: Stable: vagal maneuvers → adenosine. Unstable: synchronized cardioversion.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88456. التجميع: cardioversion

q: Child eating popcorn, then sudden continuous cough, localized wheeze and decreased air entry on one side. Diagnosis?
k: Sudden cough + unilateral wheeze → FB
r: Next: rigid bronchoscopy.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88456.

q: Unconscious person found in a burning house; burns on the face, soot at the nostrils and mouth. Diagnosis/priority?
o: Inhalation injury (and CO poisoning) → early intubation
k: Soot + facial burns → inhalation injury
r: Secure the airway early; give 100% O2 for CO poisoning.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88456.

q: Chest trauma; right side dull to percussion. Diagnosis and management?
k: Dull percussion after trauma = hemothorax
r: Chest tube; thoracotomy if >1500 mL initially or >200 mL/h.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88456.

q: Patient with fever for one month; CSF: low glucose, high protein, mainly lymphocytes. Diagnosis?
k: Chronic + lymphocytes + low glucose → TB
r: Viral: normal glucose. Bacterial: neutrophils, acute.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88456. ⚠ من الذاكرة

q: Diabetic patient develops hypertension. Best treatment?
k: DM + HTN → ACEi/ARB
r: Renal protection (albuminuria).
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88456.

q: SLE patient develops neuropsychiatric lupus. Treatment?
k: Severe organ involvement (CNS) → steroids + cyclophosphamide
r: Major organ (CNS/renal) lupus → pulse steroids + cyclophosphamide (or MMF for nephritis).
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88456.

q: RA patient on prednisolone, methotrexate and HCQ still has active disease. What to add?
k: Failed triple csDMARD → biologic
r: Persistent activity despite MTX + HCQ (+ steroid) → add a biologic (TNF inhibitor).
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88456. ⚠ باقي الخيارات منسية

q: 40-year-old, 4 months after gastric bypass, presents with diffuse abdominal pain for 12 hours; tenderness and rebound tenderness. Next step?
k: Post-bypass + peritonitis → surgery
r: Peritonitis (rebound) after bariatric surgery = leak/internal hernia → urgent surgical exploration.
n: ✔ الحمراني 15 نوفمبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88491.

q: Woman with ectopic pregnancy 2 years ago, planning to conceive. Advice?
k: Previous ectopic → early US in next pregnancy
r: Recurrence risk ~10–15% → early localization of pregnancy by ultrasound.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88457.

q: 18-year-old girl with irregular cycles and severe dysmenorrhea starting one day before menses for 3 days, missing work. Management?
k: Dysmenorrhea + irregular cycles → OCP
r: OCP treats both pain and cycle irregularity (NSAIDs are first-line for pain alone).
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88507.

q: Patient with classic acute cholangitis (fever, jaundice, RUQ pain), BP normal. Most appropriate INITIAL management?
o: IV crystalloid fluid bolus (+ IV antibiotics)
k: Cholangitis → resuscitate + antibiotics first
r: Initial: IV fluids + antibiotics. Then ERCP for decompression (definitive).
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88517. التعليقات: C

q: Woman with ectopic treated with methotrexate: β-hCG day 1 = 1000, day 4 = 1200, day 7 = 2100. Next step?
k: hCG rising after MTX → surgery
r: Expect ≥15% fall between day 4 and 7; rising hCG = failure → surgery (or second dose if stable).
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88546. التجميع: surgical

q: Surgeon doing a lipoma excision with lidocaine; patient develops tinnitus and perioral numbness. Diagnosis?
k: Tinnitus + perioral numbness = LAST
r: Stop injection, support, lipid emulsion if severe.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88546.

q: Woman after severe postpartum hemorrhage cannot breastfeed and has amenorrhea. Diagnosis?
k: PPH → no lactation → Sheehan
r: Pituitary infarction after PPH.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88546.

q: A study links BMI and systolic BP: SBP = 90 + 1.5 × BMI. Predicted SBP for BMI 30?
r: Simple linear regression substitution.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88547. التعليقات: 135

q: 9-month-old not sitting alone, can roll, no head lag when pulled up. What to do?
k: Not sitting by 9 months = red flag
r: Sitting without support is expected by ~6–8 months; not by 9 months → refer/developmental work-up.
n: سايلنت الأحد 15 #88548. التعليقات: further work-up

q: Picture of endometrial polyp. Management?
k: Endometrial polyp → hysteroscopy + polypectomy
n: ✔ التعليقات. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88549.

q: Most common cause of postpartum hemorrhage?
k: PPH = Tone > Trauma > Tissue > Thrombin
n: ✔ التعليقات. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88550.

q: Stepping reflex – when does it disappear?
k: Stepping disappears ~2 months
r: Rooting ~4 months, Moro ~4–6 months, palmar grasp ~6 months.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88551.

q: Infant with fatigue and hypotonia (hypoglycemia). Insulin 40 (high), cortisol 552 (normal), β-hydroxybutyrate 0.01 (low). Diagnosis?
k: Hypoglycemia + high insulin + low ketones → hyperinsulinism
r: Insulin suppresses ketogenesis. GSD and cortisol/GH deficiency have high ketones.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88552.

q: Type 1 diabetic in clinic is drowsy and sweating but able to swallow. Best immediate action?
k: Conscious hypoglycemia → oral glucose
r: Unable to swallow → IV dextrose or IM glucagon.
n: ✔ الجواب كتبه اللي اختبر. سايلنت الأحد 15 #88553.

q: Murmur that increases with standing and decreases with handgrip. Diagnosis?

q: A woman with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) presents with hirsutism and irregular menstrual cycles. Local cosmetic treatments have not helped. What is the most appropriate management?
r: Combined OCPs are first-line drug treatment for PCOS-related hirsutism: they raise SHBG and suppress ovarian androgens, and they also regulate the cycle. Anti-androgens (spironolactone, cyproterone, finasteride) are added after 6 months if the response is inadequate, with contraception.

q: A patient has recurrent infections. Labs show absent T cells and low serum immunoglobulins, with recurrent fungal infections and diarrhoea. What is the diagnosis?
r: Absent T cells plus low immunoglobulins (combined T- and B-cell failure), with candidiasis, chronic diarrhoea and failure to thrive in infancy, is SCID. The definitive treatment is haematopoietic stem cell transplant.
n: صورة من سايلنت الاثنين 16 – موجود في ياسر (NOV-161). Why not B? Wiskott-Aldrich gives the triad eczema + thrombocytopenia with small platelets + recurrent infections, with low IgM and initially normal T-cell numbers.
